speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic; I understand you are presenting with postmenopausal bleeding and an adnexal mass. To begin our evaluation, are you currently taking any hormone replacement therapy or other medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old woman. The patient presents with a 2-month history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding. She denies any recent weight loss, fever, or changes in bladder or bowel habits. No previous history of similar symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you; since you are not on hormone replacement therapy or other medications, let's focus on the adnexal mass. Can you describe the characteristics of this mass, such as its size, whether it is painful, or if it has caused any bloating or pressure symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Intermittent bleeding from the vagina. I also have No recent weight loss, No fever, No changes in bladder or bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometrial Hyperplasia (with or without atypia) secondary to an estrogen-secreting ovarian tumor (e.g., Granulosa cell tumor) causing an adnexal mass.

I need to confirm the size of the mass and whether it is simple or complex. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic Ultrasound. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic Ultrasound.
